text:
sam (support): FYI — Escalation from ACME (prod). They say after the Mar 10 rollout the assistant started "losing" earlier instructions in very long conversations (> ~12k tokens). Previously stable. Customer reports truncated context and worse coherence near the end. Request IDs attached: req_0a1b2c, req_0a1b2d.

olivia (customer-success): Pasting the customer's minimal repro and notes (they gave permission to share snippets). They say instructions in the system message are not being respected when the chat goes long; the user prompt at the end is ignored or answered out of scope. Example payload below.

olivia (customer-success): ```
POST /v1/chat/completions
{
  "model": "rw-infer-3.1",
  "messages": [
    {"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant that ALWAYS summarizes the last user instruction in a single line at the end of the reply."},
    /* ~12k tokens of conversation here, many assistant and user messages */
    {"role":"user","content":"Please do the one-line summary now."}
  ],
  "max_tokens": 300,
  "stream": false
}
```

olivia (customer-success): Customer attached two responses: old (before Mar10) returns a one-line summary at the end; new response either omits the summary, returns unrelated content, or truncates mid-sentence. They gave us the raw strings if needed.

deploy-bot: Deployed r-2026-03-10T02:40Z -> production (components: runtime v1.9.2, serving-kernel v7, kv-cache default-enabled, chunker v2).

mira (eng-runtime): :eyes: Thanks. First quick q: did they pin to rw-infer-3.1 or are they using a runtime alias that could have changed model variant? Also: are they using prefix caching / kv-attach?

sam (support): They said model pinned to rw-infer-3.1. No custom endpoint config in their app. Using our hosted API, default routing. No explicit cache flags.

jesse (eng-ml): Two obvious levers to check: 1) truncate strategy/default context-window change (we shipped a change to evict older KV entries earlier to reduce memory/latency), 2) tokenization/chunker change that altered token counts => effective context shorter. Both could cause earlier system prompt to be evicted.

mira (eng-runtime): I pulled the deploy diff: runtime v1.9.2 changed default KV eviction policy from LRU to time-based with aggressive compaction for >8k tokens (to reduce memory spikes). That seems likely. There's also a change in the chunker: chunker v2 packs system instructions differently which could shift where token boundaries fall.

alex (product): If KV eviction became more aggressive, that would match "instructions lost in long chats". We need to confirm whether eviction is by bytes or by message count. Also want to know if we changed the default "truncate_strategy" (head vs tail). Customer expects system to persist to the end.

mira (eng-runtime): Repro plan I suggest: 1) run a synthetic chat with a long history (~13k tokens) with a distinctive system instruction at the start and a pointed final user instruction; 2) compare responses against pre-deploy runtime (v1.9.1) and post-deploy (v1.9.2). Use the same tokenizer and measure where eviction occurred.

jesse (eng-ml): Here's a small repro curl you can run locally against staging and prod (adjust keys):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"model":"rw-infer-3.1","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"INSTRUCT: always include the token SUMMARY: <S>"}, %LONG_HISTORY_PLACEHOLDER%, {"role":"user","content":"Return SUMMARY now."}], "max_tokens": 256}'
```

mira (eng-runtime): Also capture token-level traces from the runtime: enable trace flag in the request header `X-Debug-Trace: 1` (will output eviction events and kv-cache hits). If we see "evict head" around token N that's our smoking gun.

sam (support): Customer can run staging repro but asked if we can repro internally first. They gave a sample long-history file (30k characters).

mira (eng-runtime): I'll run it on prod traffic-mirroring node and compare with a node pinned to v1.9.1. If we reproduce, we need to decide rollback or config tweak. My bet: default eviction window reduced too aggressively.

jesse (eng-ml): Another fast mitigation: change truncate strategy to "tail-preserve-system" (we don't have that as a public flag yet, but we can flip the runtime config to prefer preserving system tokens over older assistant history). If that works we can hotpatch config while we sort a root fix.

alex (product): Prioritize this high. Customer is on paid Dedicated plan? (if yes we might want to offer SLA credit and fast rollback).

olivia (customer-success): ACME is mid-market currently on paid plan. They were clear they need predictability; they're open to a temporary rollback.

mira (eng-runtime): Quick check-in: I ran the repro on a staging node pinned to v1.9.2. Trace shows: `evict_count=640 evicted_tokens=512 strategy=time_compact reason=memory_pressure` at approx token index 10124. The system token block was at token 400. That eviction doc suggests we're evicting earlier context segments (head-first).

jesse (eng-ml): That aligns. Outcome: system instruction getting evicted before final user request => model no longer has the rule to summarize. Also chunker v2 changed token offsets so the system block sits in a different bucket which gets evicted earlier.

mira (eng-runtime): Proposed immediate actions: 
- Hotpatch runtime config on prod to reduce compaction aggressiveness (set time_compact threshold -> higher)
- Add temporary policy to prefer preserving system & recent user messages (policy: preserve_system=1)
- Run canary patch against 5% traffic and validate with customer's repro.

alex (product): Approve canary. If canary fixes repro, we do full rollout. If not, rollback to v1.9.1. Also inform CS to offer SLA credit.

sam (support): I'll spin up the canary run, coordinate with Olivia to run customer's test against canary. Olivia, can you get the customer to test in next 2 hours?

olivia (customer-success): Reached out, they can test in 3 hours. I'll pipeline their sample into our canary validation harness.

mira (eng-runtime): Patching now to add `preserve_system=1` on canary nodes. Canary ID c-2026-03-11T09:45Z.

deploy-bot: Canary c-2026-03-11T09:45Z applied to 5% of traffic (nodes: node-47, node-89).

mira (eng-runtime): Early results: customer's synthetic run against canary produced correct one-line summary. No eviction events for the system block in trace.

jesse (eng-ml): Good signal. We should also add an automated regression test in the eval harness: long-context preserve_system test with 10k/15k/20k token histories. If that passes we avoid future regressions.

alex (product): Agreed — ticketing: PLAT-2026-891 for rollback/hotpatch + PLAT-2026-892 for long-context eval coverage.

sam (support): Noted. I'll keep the customer updated. Great triage team. :thumbsup:

olivia (customer-success): Customer confirmed canary fixed their sample. They're happy to wait for full rollout and want confirmation when it's live.

mira (eng-runtime): Plan for full rollout in 2 hours if no other issues. We'll also revert chunker v2 if risk remains, but initial canary suggests config tweak is sufficient.

alex (product): After rollout, we should send a short postmortem to the customer explaining root cause (kv-cache compaction + chunker offset change), steps taken, and long-term mitigations (eval suite + config flags exposed).

sam (support): Closing loop: I'll update the ticket once full rollout completes. If anyone wants the raw traces or request IDs, ping me and I'll attach them.

mira (eng-runtime): Attaching one trace snippet here for internal folks: ```
trace_id=req_0a1b2c
kv_events:
  hit=1284 miss=32 evict=640 evicted_tokens=512
evict_policy=time_compact threshold=8k result=evict_head
```

jesse (eng-ml): We'll add a model-side guard too — if system instructions are absent in context, produce a short disclaimer instead of hallucinating. That helps customer UX while infra fix is in flight.

alex (product): Thanks team. Postmortem owner: olivia + mira. SLA comms: sam. Engineering fix owner: mira + jesse.

sam (support): Thread summary: Regression after 2026-03-10 rollout due to kv-cache compaction + chunker token offset change -> system prompt eviction in long contexts. Canary patch `preserve_system=1` fixed customer repro. Rolling out to prod in 2 hours.

olivia (customer-success): I'll draft the customer note once prod rollout complete.

mira (eng-runtime): I'll post an ops note in #eng-runtime when full rollout finishes and attach regression test results.

sam (support): Thanks all.
